clue.text: Fall of assassin that's central to Ides

parts.note: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar

indicators.note: what is central to a word is its middle, so only the inner letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of Ides

explanation.surface: A Roman conspirator's downfall, tied to the Ides of March when Caesar was murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caesar setting makes 'Fall' look like the assassin's ruin; it is the definition, a noun for falling water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, water falling in stages down rocks, so a fall in that sense.

clue.text: Hit hard and take into custody

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strike with the hand

explanation.surface: A police officer roughing up a suspect while arresting them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff is to strike someone with an open hand, and also informal for handcuffing an arrested person.

clue.text: Founder of NSYNC vocalised after Justin finally left

indicators.note: something that has left is gone, so that letter's sound is removed
vocalised means spoken, so the band name is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the boy band's name is pronounced like the letter N followed by a word for a basin

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name before it

parts.note: last letter of Justin

explanation.surface: The band founding member left after Justin Timberlake went solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like the person who started NSYNC; it is the verb. NSYNC is an American boy band whose lead singer was Justin Timberlake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that founders fills with water and goes down, so it sinks.

clue.text: Around start of G7, America seceded? Nonsense, B.S. and more

indicators.note: the following words go around that single letter, enclosing it
nonsense makes no sense as ordered, so the letters must be rearranged to make sense

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a name is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first character of G7

explanation.surface: A political fantasy that the US quit the G7 group of nations, dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: B.S. is the American abbreviation for a Bachelor of Science; the British write BSc. The question mark flags the absurd political premise.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bachelor of Science is one university qualification, and masters and doctorates are more of them.

clue.text: Animal on which Darwin rode, starting out

indicators.note: with its start out, the first letter of the ship's name is removed

parts.note: Charles Darwin sailed round the world on HMS Beagle

explanation.surface: Recalling the vessel Darwin travelled on when first setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal on which Darwin rode' suggests a horse or tortoise; the animal is the definition, and what he rode was a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey, and birds are animals.

clue.text: Casper travels a long way

indicators.note: a name that travels moves about, so its letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Casper, perhaps the friendly ghost, goes on a lengthy journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of distance of about 3.26 light years, certainly a long way.

clue.text: Insane psychopath arose where chemist's seen

indicators.note: insane means deranged, so the letters lose their order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deranged killer emerges at the local pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was an old-fashioned pharmacist, so his shop is where a chemist (pharmacist) would be found.

clue.text: Stinking initials B.O. elicit sound of disapproval

indicators.note: something stinking is rotten, so the letters are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, dots dropped

explanation.surface: The letters B.O. for body odour provoke a hiss of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: B.O. is body odour, which explains the 'Stinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibilation is a hissing sound, the noise an audience makes to show it disapproves.

clue.text: A 'queen' may do this with snappy ornamentation

parts.note: someone snappy is irritable, cross
to dress is to adorn, as in dressing a window or a tree

explanation.surface: A drag queen pairing a sharp outfit with elaborate accessories.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'queen' point to a drag queen, not royalty. Snappy looks like stylish but means bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag queens perform in women's clothes, wearing the garments of the opposite sex.

clue.text: Dance nut beginning to dance a dance without an introduction

indicators.note: with no introduction the opening letter is dropped from the named dance

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept of the next word

parts.note: first letter of dance
the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A jumble of dance instructions about a dance-mad enthusiast starting a dance, word repeated to dizzy effect.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'dance' three times, the first is the definition, the second supplies its first letter, and the third is the tango beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, performed with castanets.

clue.text: 'You're awful! You're terrible! Stupid mistake!'

parts.note: a boo is the jeer that tells a performer they are awful
another jeer at a terrible act

explanation.surface: Someone berating a person who has just blundered, exclamation after exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two insults are each the sound an audience makes to say so.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo-boo is an informal word for a silly blunder or embarrassing error.

clue.text: Unclear that king covered in Times

indicators.note: a thing covered in something has that something wrapped around it on both sides

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in four by three
King Lear of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A vague complaint that some monarch was written up in the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and blurred, so things look unclear.

clue.text: A singing brother by hotel, drowning in expenses in fancy area

indicators.note: something drowning in a liquid is surrounded by it, so these pieces sit inside the word for expenses

parts.note: bills are expenses to pay
Don and Phil Everly were the Everly Brothers, a 1950s-60s singing duo
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A famous singer, staying at a hotel, swamped by charges in some smart neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drowning in expenses' reads as being swamped by costs, but it places the singer and hotel inside the word for expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverly Hills is the wealthy Los Angeles enclave synonymous with luxury living, a posh district.

clue.text: Yank, engrossed by clue for bloodhound, sits nervously for investigators

indicators.note: a nervous person fidgets, so these letters shift into a new order
to be engrossed by something is to be absorbed into it, so this goes inside

parts.note: a bloodhound tracks by scent
Yank is the setter, so the setter's pronoun I
sits rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter, absorbed by a puzzle about a tracking dog, waits anxiously for detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to themself by their pseudonym, here Yank, giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists investigate the natural world through experiments, so they are researchers or investigators.

clue.text: Freed in error, Pierce is a spewer of venom

indicators.note: letters in error are wrongly placed and need putting into the right order

parts.note: freed rearranged
to lance is to pierce, as with a boil

explanation.surface: A prisoner named Pierce, released by mistake, rants bitterly.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierce looks like a man's name; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The fer-de-lance is a highly venomous Central and South American pit viper.

clue.text: Revolutionary diarist with peak wine

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
Anaïs Nin, famous for her published diaries
Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps

explanation.surface: A revolutionary and a writer sharing a top-quality wine together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak wine' reads as excellent wine, but peak is Mont Blanc and wine alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenin blanc is a white grape variety from the Loire, and the white wine made from it.

clue.text: Prohibition on headgear for fowl

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
a tam, or tam-o'-shanter, is a Scottish woollen cap

explanation.surface: A rule forbidding hats on chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A on B puts A above B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken, a kind of fowl.

clue.text: Besmirch quisling in retreat

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a rat is a traitor, like the Norwegian collaborator Quisling

explanation.surface: Blackening the name of a traitor who is fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tar someone is to smear their reputation, as in tarring with the same brush.

clue.text: Barrie heroine stripped off, showing rear

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters of the name go

parts.note: Wendy Darling is the heroine of J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A storybook heroine undressing and revealing her backside, a cheeky picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of something is its back part, the rear or tail end.

clue.text: Marie's singing brother Mel in wild brawls

parts.note: Donny Osmond, singing brother of Marie Osmond
Mel Brooks, the comedy film director

explanation.surface: Two American entertainers caught up in a wild punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A donnybrook is a chaotic free-for-all fight, named after a rowdy Dublin fair.

clue.text: Rap sheet torn apart with glee in terse language

indicators.note: something torn apart is broken into bits that can be put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
glee taken as written, added by with

explanation.surface: Someone happily ripping up their criminal record, described in few words.
explanation.walkthrough: A rap sheet is an American term for a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegraphese is the clipped style of telegrams, where words were charged individually, so clipped and brief.

clue.text: Theft of cuckoo shite

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go wild into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stealing the droppings of a cuckoo, a crude and silly crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Shite is British vulgar slang for excrement.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially a large, carefully planned one.

clue.text: Bear's shown up in circus apparatus

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear of A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A bear performing in a circus ring with props.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoops are rings used by circus performers and animals to jump through or spin.

clue.text: Stick together with fool

definitions.meaning: first meaning: thicken into a lump, as blood does

explanation.surface: Advice to stay loyal to a silly friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Clot as a fool is British informal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood clots by congealing into a mass, and a clot is a British word for a stupid person.

clue.text: Pick up one teacher

parts.note: to pick up something is to detect or sense it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Collecting a single teacher, say from school.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensei is the Japanese title for a teacher or martial-arts master.

clue.text: Later, he's active close to outskirts of Whitehall

parts.note: nigh means near or close
taken as written

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters of the name are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Whitehall

explanation.surface: A civil servant who keeps working late on the edge of Whitehall, the London street of government offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as one phrase meaning near; here it is split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who is most alert and active late into the night.

clue.text: Tip reduced by 1/3? Crikey!

indicators.note: cutting a word by a third removes a third of its letters, here the front portion

parts.note: baksheesh is a tip or gratuity, a word from the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone shocked at a gratuity cut by a third.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine-letter word for a tip loses three letters, BAK, from its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheesh is an exclamation of exasperation or surprise, like the British crikey.

clue.text: Great position, any way you look at it

indicators.text: any way you look at it
indicators.note: a word that is the same whichever way you look reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: a leading place, which reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: An enviable place, however you view it.
explanation.definitionFit: The top spot is first place, the most prestigious ranking in any list.
